posts.text:
The American people gave us a mandate to lower costs, and BAAJA is our first major opportunity to deliver.

Let's get it passed.

https://t.co/ktwUmTmNfG

It’s going to take a huge step towards solving the affordability crisis and setting us on a path of energy abundance.

The Senate is taking its first votes on this package today. It should be passed ASAP and the House should stand ready to send it to the President’s desk.

Any project that’s illegal today will also be illegal after passage. BAAJA just makes it faster to come to that decision (not to mention requiring data centers to pay much higher costs). 

This is a strong deal that’s been made even better after the managers amendment.

A second objection is that this bill will allow currently illegal projects to move forward, like allowing data centers to be built in national parks. 

This is patently untrue.

Opponents argue there will be some better deal in the future. But Trump remains in the White House, and I don’t think there’s any other deal for the next two years. 

We should pass this bill now, and if we can improve it after 2028, we should do that too!

There are also a ton of extra wins to this package - adding nuclear, making data centers pay their fair share, establishing new support for communities near these projects - all while cutting power sector CO2 emissions by 20%.

The manager’s amendment addresses tribal concerns around reforms to NHPA while protecting tribal sovereignty, balancing project certainty with future review, and making transmission development more flexible and workable for states and developers.

The Senate permitting deal makes it easier to build all types of energy by delivering certainty for builders, streamlining reviews, and expanding enforcement mechanisms. 

The manager’s amendment released over the weekend takes this deal a step further.

Energy costs rose 33% over the last 5 years. Projects are being tied down by 3+ years of reviews. And recent analysis shows permitting costs $12 billion every single year. 

The only sustainable way to lower electricity prices for businesses and consumers is to build more energy.

Last week, voters sent a clear message that the status quo isn’t working. Today, as the Senate starts votes on the permitting deal, we have a chance to change that. 

It’s rare we get to lower costs, create jobs & cut climate emissions all at once. We can’t miss this opportunity.
Great to sit down with @JeremiahDJohns and @CNLiberalism to talk about the need to build more in America. An affordable future depends on it. https://t.co/bHVj0xU8HM
Clean energy projects shouldn't have to worry about political interference every step of the way. Projects need certainty, not political games. https://t.co/ZP9wAYuLXu

Momentum is growing for making it easier to build, especially housing and energy.

What we need now is acceleration. I sat down with @DKThomp to talk about the Build America Caucus’ vision for delivering broad prosperity.
https://t.co/Kv8Z618ai4
America spends more on healthcare than any other country, all despite families not being able to find or afford quality care. The Build More Agenda is fixing that: https://t.co/h8RvJPfuEa
America has gotten way too bad at building the things Americans need. @RepMaloyUtah and I just announced a bipartisan plan to fix that. https://t.co/J3sEFBV1FY

The fastest way to restore faith in government and the promise of life in America is to build something real that people can feel, and that’s what this agenda is all about.

We invite you to join us in bringing both sides together and making life better!

https://t.co/ysZSqsUFaH

We know that this vision for American life depends on a government that can actually deliver.

So we’re going to get new talent hired, cut out bureaucratic waste, and ensure that government can be agile and proactive to your kitchen-table concerns.

From childcare to the classroom to finding a career, Americans should find opportunity at every step. But too often government gets in the way. 

Our plan cuts red tape that limits childcare, invests in effective teaching, and removes barriers that keep skilled people out of work.

But fixing the government failures you face every day remains top of mind.

Every pothole and construction delay reminds us how hard it is to build in America.

We’re changing that by fast-tracking approvals for more projects and ensuring they’re finished on time.

We’re going to double the pace of American science within a decade.

How? Permanently authorizing the Genesis Mission to connect the nation’s science infrastructure under one discovery-focused platform.

On energy, we must pass the permitting certainty deal, invest smarter in our energy grid, and build out the next-generation power portfolio America deserves.

That’s going to ensure prices come down and stay down for the long haul.

Healthcare provider shortages are another huge concern.

We’re going to close those gaps by changing how Medicare invests in physician training to prioritize the communities with the greatest need, and we’re going to make sure their time is spent on patient care, not paperwork.

Take housing - one-third of young adults under 30 still live with their parents because they can’t afford to go anywhere else.

Solving that means getting more homes built by fully implementing the recent federal housing law, and going a step further on financing, construction costs, and innovative supply solutions.

We know that this agenda won’t fix everything. 

What we are prioritizing is a home you can afford, care when you need it, cheaper power, faster cures and breakthroughs, infrastructure that actually gets built, and more opportunity from every age.

What we need now is acceleration, especially at this critical moment in time.

We’ve become a nation that struggles to build, and we have a responsibility to cut the red tape and waste standing in the way of our ability to grow again. 

That’s where this agenda comes in.

And we succeeded in spurring a deal on tech-neutral permitting certainty that will get more projects built, reduce foreign dependence, and drive down costs for our families.

That permitting deal still needs to be passed, and it should if we're serious about lowering costs.

We also helped negotiate and pass the biggest policy win of this Congress and the strongest pro-supply housing package in half a century.

The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act is going to lower costs, jumpstart new construction, and cut costly red tape - it faced a ton of hurdles, but we’re incredibly excited to see it finally become law.

And we’ve had some real successes over the past year.

We’ve grown to over 40 members and added conservatives and progressives alike to our ranks, united around frustration at how difficult it's become to not just pass solutions but see those impacts materialize back home.

The Build America Caucus was founded last year to bring both parties together to clear away the red tape and waste that’s standing in the way of accomplishing these goals.

We may not agree on everything, but we believe that America works best when we can build the things we need.

The problem is the federal government hasn’t gotten onboard enough.

And the truth is we need federal action to do big things like build more homes, make it easier to get new energy projects connected to the grid, and keep American innovation competitive with China.

The good news is that pro-growth mentality has been bubbling in cities and states across the country for years.

Places like Austin and Jacksonville have proven that prices stabilize when housing supply expands.

Utah is leading the West in a “Superabundance” strategy to develop widely available and affordable energy.

But to actually change any of this, we need a new politics of action focused on making government work better, not two more years of bitter partisan fights.

That’s the case that Co-Chair @RepMaloyUtah and I made in @Politico today. 

https://t.co/ZbyeF0OIsK

Government’s ability to solve kitchen-table issues is broken. We all know this.

Mortgages, rents, and power bills are too high, and good doctors, great daycares, and high-paying jobs are all too hard to find.

🚨HUGE NEWS:  The Build America Caucus is launching an ambitious, bipartisan agenda focused on improving Americans’ lives by making it easier to build the things we need.

It just went live on our website for you to read. Here’s why you should: 🧵

https://t.co/zT1pzVBYes

Getting to this point is a huge victory, and like the federal housing law we passed this summer, it’s exactly the kind of pro-growth win that the Build America Caucus has been pushing for.

Let’s keep it up and send this to the President’s desk ASAP.

The Senate’s bipartisan permitting bill addresses all of these issues. 

It’s a serious effort at trying to solve the problems that have been keeping energy projects from getting built for years.

Add to that a host of other laws that can slow down the process and an aging grid system that can’t keep up with the energy we want to bring online.

If you want to transition to a clean energy economy, you should want to fix these problems ASAP.

roll_calls.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Housing for the 21st Century Act (H R 6644)
roll_calls.plain_language: This bill establishes and modifies various federal housing programs. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

roll_calls.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Concur in Senate Adt to House Adt to Senate Adt — Housing for the 21st Century Act (H R 6644)
roll_calls.plain_language: The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act establishes and modifies various federal housing programs. This vote, under suspension of the rules, was on accepting the Senate's latest changes to the bill after the chambers traded versions, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea accepts the Senate's version; a Nay opposes it.
